articles.author: Joel Rose
articles.description: Three days after a communications meltdown led the FAA to ground planes, there are big questions about what happened and how much money is needed to upgrade the country's air traffic control system.
articles.title: Questions about FAA funding roil Capitol Hill after nationwide ground stop

articles.author: Huo Jingnan
articles.description: The state's attorney general started investigating OpenAI after the Hugging Face attack and now says this attack was "entirely foreseeable" due to OpenAI's poor security practices.
articles.title: California sues OpenAI over hacking risks

articles.author: Glen Weldon
articles.description: Amazon announced Monday that Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond. NPR critic Glen Weldon says the idiosyncratic actor would seem to be a better fit as a Bond villain.
articles.title: If Robert Pattinson is James Bond, 007 needs to get a little weird

articles.author: Erika Ryan
articles.description: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer talks with James Fallows about his reporting on the safety of air travel, published in the New York Times Magazine the day before the nationwide ground stop.
articles.title: Pilot and journalist says fault lines beginning to show in U.S. air travel

articles.author: Katie McQue
articles.description: The new rule closes a loophole that existed that allowed Chinese companies to still access advanced AI chips remotely, despite U.S. restrictions on their physical sale to China.
articles.title: U.S. tightens controls on remote access to AI technology amid Nvidia fallout

articles.author: Imogen Foulkes
articles.description: Countries are meeting in Geneva to negotiate rules on weapons that can select and kill targets without human intervention. But with the U.S., Russia and Israel resisting legally binding controls, campaigners fear the window to act is closing.
articles.title: U.N. talks seek to rein in 'killer robots' as fears over AI weapons grow

articles.author: John Powers
articles.description: Adam Driver, Scarlett Johansson and Miles Teller star in a film that isn't merely one of this year's very best films; it possesses a weight and depth you rarely find in American movies anymore.
articles.title: A family runs afoul of the Russian mob in the terrific 'Paper Tiger'

articles.author: Jennifer Vanasco
articles.description: "We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007," Denis Villeneuve, who will direct the new Bond film, said in an announcement from Amazon MGM Studios.
articles.title: Robert Pattinson is the next James Bond

articles.author: Bill Chappell
articles.description: A new trial is set in Massachusetts against Lindsay Clancy as prosecutors seek a criminal conviction over the killing of her three young children.
articles.title: Lindsay Clancy to face a new trial in spring of 2027 over children's killing

articles.author: Hazel Cills
articles.description: The nominations for the 69th annual Grammy Awards were announced on Monday, and women artists across genres rule the major categories.
articles.title: RAYE and Rosalía lead the 2027 Grammy nominations

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
As tourism booms, three experienced female travellers give their take on how to make the most of travelling here
The 13th-century Persian scholar Zakariyya al-Qazwini never travelled to India. But he catalogued it in his famous work The Wonders of Creation and Rarities of Existence, which drew on accounts of a distant land filled with “rarities par excellence”. For al-Qazwini, as Helen Pfeifer writes in the London Review of Books, wonder was not an emotion but an intellectual method of making sense of the world and acquiring knowledge.
India has long occupied such a space in the global imagination, as a land of extraordinary riches; spirituality, customs, chaos and contradictions. This has shaped how the country is perceived from afar, but it can often flatten its complexities.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India has been named a ‘destination of the year’ for 2027 – here are insiders’ tips on travelling beyond the tropes

articles.author: Phillip Inman
articles.description:
Wage growth falls to to 3.5% in September, as ministers examine how best to get young people into work

Milburn urges Burnham to spend billions on young people

Who are the Neets? UK youth job crisis in five charts

The UK unemployment rate has unexpectedly fallen as the government prepares to release a major report on the youth jobs crisis.
The unemployment rate was 4.6% in September, dipping from 4.7% in August, according to the Office for National Statistics. City economists had expected it to remain at 4.7%.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK unemployment unexpectedly eases to 4.6%, as government prepares to release Milburn report

articles.author: Lauren Almeida
articles.description:
New tech wealth, amassed with remarkable speed, is now washing up on British shores
Sporting hoodies and white trainers rather than the gilets of London’s banker and lawyer class, tech bros can struggle to be taken seriously by the capital’s luxury property agents. “We worked with a young tech entrepreneur with a substantial budget, who agents assumed was looking to rent a one-bedroom flat,” says Jo Eccles, a buying agent who sources off-market properties for ultra-wealthy clients.
But this week’s float by Anthropic, the AI developer behind the chatbot Claude, promises to bring even more credibility for the growing cohort of tech millionaires, which could breathe life into London’s ailing high-end property market. Its IPO on Thursday, expected to value the company at $1.4tn (£1.1m), is likely to turn more than 4,000 of its staff into millionaires as their stock options vest.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Millionaire factory: Anthropic IPO set to fuel AI gold rush in London’s high-end property market

articles.author: Jordyn Beazley
articles.description:
So You Are placed eighth in race just two weeks ago and was put down after a severe bout of colic

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The body of a horse that placed eighth in Australia’s Melbourne Cup two weeks ago and recently fell ill has been found dumped in skip bin in Sydney.
The horse So You Are, a five-year-old gelding, was put down after it suffered from a severe bout from colic and was taken to hospital on Monday for surgery.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Disgusted by it’: body of Melbourne Cup race horse found dumped in Sydney skip bin

articles.author: Tom McIlroy in Manila
articles.description:
Organisers say up to 10,000 people could join the next round of demonstrations ahead of the US president’s arrival in Manila for the Asean summit

Asean and Apec summits – live updates

Hundreds of people have been arrested in heated demonstrations against Donald Trump in Manila, as authorities braced for more protests ahead of the US president’s arrival in the city for a leaders’ summit.
Organisers claim as many as 10,000 people will join protests against Trump in the Philippine capital on Tuesday, when he will attend the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit. The crowds are expected to try to walk to the summit site.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hundreds arrested in anti-Trump protests in Philippines amid anger over Iran war and AI pact

articles.author: Susan Chenery
articles.description:
Inquest continues into deaths of four babies born in free births or home births in northern rivers 

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A northern rivers mother whose baby died after a free birth did not know she was having twins until she was in labour after having no pregnancy scans, the New South Wales coroner’s court has heard.
The inquest will examine the deaths of four babies born in free births or home births who died in the northern rivers region between 2022 and 2024. It will consider whether the care was reasonable in the circumstances and whether care by an unregistered support worker was reasonable and appropriate before, during and after the birth. Free births are when a person gives birth without a registered health professional present.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Woman whose baby died after free birth didn’t know she was pregnant with twins, NSW inquest hears

articles.author: Jonathan Barrett and Luca Ittimani
articles.description:
Upmarket retailer, which recorded a net loss of $228m last financial year, has total debt over $400m including $11m owed to staff 

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Upmarket retailer David Jones owed hundreds of millions of dollars when it collapsed into administration, after accelerating financial losses and reputational damage threatened its ability to stock shelves for Christmas.
About 500 creditors attended its first meeting on Tuesday, where administrators McGrathNicol started to break down who is owed what, when those left out of pocket will know where they stand, and what ultimately went wrong.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: David Jones: what went wrong and what happens next? Five takeaways from first creditors meeting

articles.author: Douglas Smith Indigenous affairs reporter
articles.description:
The NSW transport department says passenger safety is its ‘highest priority’ and the driver is no longer employed by the operator

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Transport for NSW is investigating allegations that a young Aboriginal mother and her family were told to leave a bus and left by the side of a regional highway because her 22-month-old child was crying.
Wiradjuri woman Kaneesha Lee Williams was travelling home from Sydney to the Riverina town of Darlington Point, 155km west of Wagga Wagga, with her young daughter, Audria, and her mother, Tamara, on Sunday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Aboriginal mother allegedly kicked off a bus in regional NSW because her baby was crying

articles.author: Matthew Pearce
articles.description:
About a third of cases involved chemicals banned for use on EU farms, according to investigation by Unearthed and Public Eye 
Pesticides sold by European chemical companies were named in more than 1,600 poisoning reports in Brazil last year, an investigation has found.
About a third of the cases involved chemicals banned from use on farms in the EU because of the risks they pose to people and the environment. But European companies are not banned from manufacturing these chemicals, as long as they export them overseas to countries where they are legally allowed to be used.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: European-made pesticides named in 1,605 poisoning reports in Brazil last year

articles.author: Fiona Harvey and Simon Evans in Antalya
articles.description:
Analysis of fossil fuel exports since 1850 differs from most assessments – which look at countries where CO2 is released
Russia, Saudi Arabia and Australia are the three biggest exporters of carbon dioxide in history, according to analysis of fossil fuels since 1850.
Russia tops the list of global exporters of fossil fuels, with its vast coal, oil and gas deposits. Accounting for the CO2 produced by burning these exports, Russia has been responsible for more than 70 gigatonnes, up to the end of 2025.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russia, Saudi Arabia and Australia named as biggest CO2 exporters in history

articles.author: Diane Taylor
articles.description:
Many of those onboard are being deported for second time after fleeing threats from people smugglers in France
Many of the asylum seekers on Tuesday’s final “one in, one out” deportation flight are people who returned to the UK fleeing threats from smugglers after they were already forcibly returned to France.
Hundreds of asylum seekers who were sent back to France are thought to have returned to the UK, citing threats from smugglers who said their families still owed them money for the Channel crossing.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Asylum seekers on final ‘one in, one out’ UK-France flight feel they are being ‘punished’

articles.author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
articles.description:
Campaigners call for reopening of high-speed Eurostar stations and new infrastructure for London St Pancras
Britain should throw its weight behind international rail services to reset the UK-EU relationship, transport campaigners have urged the prime minister.
A coalition of groups has called on Andy Burnham to commit to reopening high-speed stations for Eurostar and other services in Kent, and to support new infrastructure for passengers at London St Pancras and for rail freight.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Invest in international rail services to boost UK-EU reset, Burnham urged

articles.author: Guy de Launey in Belgrade
articles.description:
Inaugural parliamentary session comes as ousted populist Aleksandar Vučić threatens mass protests of his own
Candidates for Serbia’s Student List, the grassroots movement of political outsiders that pulled off a spectacular victory in last month’s elections over the party of the populist leader Aleksandar Vučić, are to be sworn in as MPs as they begin the process of forming a government.
The 140 candidates – among them academics, lawyers, scientists and the odd actor – will be sworn in on Tuesday during the inaugural session of the new parliament, bringing 14 years of rule by Vučić and his Serbian Progressive party (SNS) to an end.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Serbia’s Student List candidates to be sworn in as MPs after election triumph

articles.author: Lucy Campbell
articles.description:
Airline acknowledges ‘technology issue that delayed flight departures’ in latest high-profile outage to affect Americans
United ⁠Airlines said on ⁠Monday ⁠that it had resolved ⁠a widespread system ⁠outage, just three days after the Federal ⁠Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop on all US flights.
“We have resolved a technology issue that delayed flight departures. While some flights were delayed, there was no impact on flights in progress, or on United Express flights,” Chicago-based United said in a statement. “There is no indication that this was a cybersecurity-related issue.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: United Airlines says ‘widespread’ system outage resolved

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Labor leader was remembered for her advocacy and co-founding union that would become United Farm Workers
California officials paid tribute to Dolores Huerta, one of the nation’s most influential labor leaders, civil rights icons and feminist activists, at a memorial ceremony Monday at the state capitol.
They remembered her as a relentless advocate for a more just and fair world. Huerta co-founded a union that became the United Farm Workers with César Chávez and made famous her rallying cry, “Sí, se puede!” – which translates to “Yes, it can be done!”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Dolores Huerta honored in ceremony at California state capitol

articles.author: Cecilia Nowell, Maanvi Singh, Shrai Popat, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Sign up for the Breaking News US email

Lauren Almeida and Dan Milmo
Elon Musk and a host of other tech bosses have called for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement at Nvidia, amid reports the former chief executive is already plotting a return to the chip company just four days after his resignation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump defends commerce secretary Lutnick for allegedly slow-walking Nvidia chip export restrictions – as it happened

articles.author: Ben Doherty
articles.description:
Community leader says fund gives chance to find solutions to ‘huge problems we have been living with since the days of the mine’s operation’
Anglo-Australian miner Rio Tinto has agreed to pay a quarter-of-a-billion dollars to begin the clean-up of the toxic Panguna mine site it abandoned more than three decades ago.
Panguna, once one of the world’s most profitable gold and copper mines, was shuttered in 1989 after violent protests over environmental damage and the inequitable division of the mine’s profits sparked a decade-long civil war on the Papua New Guinean island of Bougainville.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rio Tinto agrees to pay US$250m to begin repairing ‘devastation’ left by Panguna mine

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Knit hat caught in ceiling fan and flung into enclosure eaten by Fiona, who is being closely monitored by zoo staff
The Cincinnati zoo says Fiona, its beloved hippo who became a global celebrity after her premature birth nearly a decade ago, is undergoing veterinary care after swallowing a knit hat that got into her enclosure.
Zoo veterinarians and staff are monitoring Fiona and working to help her pass the hat, the zoo said in a statement Monday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fiona the hippo under veterinary care after eating hat at Cincinnati zoo

articles.author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
articles.description:
Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’
Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.
The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s newly agreed returns law that allows people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda

articles.author: Cecilia Nowell
articles.description:
Hatchlings emerge after discovery in September of first sea turtle nests ever to have been recorded on US west coast
Two months after the discovery of the first sea turtle nests ever to have been recorded on the US west coast, the eggs have hatched – and California’s first group of 75 native-born olive ridley sea turtles have been released into the Pacific.
The eggs incubated at the Aquarium of the Pacific in Long Beach after the historic discovery of two separate nests in September at southern California beaches, a shift likely driven by this year’s El Niño conditions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Band of baby sea turtles swims into ocean after historic California nesting

articles.author: Richard Partington, Kiran Stacey and Aletha Adu
articles.description:
Report on Britain’s youth jobs crisis calls for welfare, education, health and employment policy shake-up
Andy Burnham is being urged to spend billions of pounds on a “new deal” for the next generation that would fund guaranteed jobs support for young people to offset a radical cut in benefits.
In a watershed report on Britain’s youth jobs crisis, Alan Milburn, the Tony Blair-era health secretary, said the country was at a “fork in the road” after a surge in the number of young people not in education, employment or training (Neet) to almost a million.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alan Milburn urges Burnham to spend billions on ‘new deal’ for young people

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
The US president oscillates between strike threats on Iran and insisting the war ‘militarily is effectively over’
A third US aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East, US Central Command said in a social media post on Monday, making a dramatic show of military might as Donald Trump keeps his options open for next steps in the Iran war.
The USS Theodore Roosevelt brings thousands of additional troops to the Middle East as Trump has oscillated between threatening additional large-scale strikes on Iran and insisting that the more than eight-month-old war “militarily is effectively over”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Third US aircraft carrier brings thousands more troops to Middle East

articles.author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
articles.description:
Home Office plans will cause unnecessary distress and anxiety, say refugee charities
Asylum seekers who have exhausted the formal appeals process will be stripped of a five-day grace period and become eligible for immediate removal under Home Office plans condemned as “distressing” by refugee charities.
Shabana Mahmood, the home secretary, will amend a bill currently before parliament to allow immigration enforcement officers to detain and remove people who have unsuccessfully appealed against their asylum or immigration claim being rejected without further notice.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Refused UK asylum seekers to lose five-day grace period and face immediate removal

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Accusations of incompetence follow retreat of Riyadh-backed forces in effort to relieve siege of Taiz and protect Aden 
Saudi Arabia has been accused by anti-Houthi forces over its military strategy after its Yemeni allies withdrew troops from the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait and pulled back forces from parts of Marib in the central part of the country.
The Saudi-backed government explained the repositioning by saying the strategic priority was to break the attritional siege on Taiz, Yemen’s third city, and to protect Aden, the southern port city in which the Saudi-backed and UN-recognised government is now based.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Saudi Arabia strategy challenged by anti-Houthi forces in Yemen

articles.author: Guardian sport
articles.description:
Suspect named as Greene Da’monte Khiree

Drug smuggling carries life sentence in Nigeria

An American basketball player has been arrested in Nigeria for allegedly attempting to smuggle 33.95kg (75lb) of marijuana into the country.
Nigeria’s National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said a 28-year-old player named as Greene Da’monte Khiree from the state of Georgia was arrested at Lagos’s main airport last Wednesday after he arrived on a flight from Thailand via the United Arab Emirates.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US basketball player arrested with 75lb of marijuana at Nigerian airport, say authorities

articles.author: Luke Harding in Kyiv
articles.description:
Traffic temporarily restricted on key connection after bridge targeted during overnight drone barrage by Ukraine
Ukraine has hit the Kerch bridge connecting occupied Crimea with Russia, in a symbolic blow that temporarily paralysed road traffic and left thousands of drivers stranded.
A Ukrainian kamikaze drone crashed into one of the bridge’s arches at 5.38am local time, local channels reported. Earlier drones could be heard buzzing above the structure, as Russian air defence units opened fire.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ukraine hits Kerch bridge between Russia and occupied Crimea

articles.author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
articles.description:
French actor apologises to two women he was convicted of assaulting on a film set in 2021
The French actor Gérard Depardieu has dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set, and has for the first time apologised to the victims.
“I was found guilty. I hear it and I accept this conviction,” Depardieu, 77, said in a written statement. “I address my deep and sincere apologies to those who suffered.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Gérard Depardieu drops appeal against sexual assault conviction

articles.author: Imran Lodhi, as told to Morgan Krakow
articles.description:
When the floods hit Pakistan he went out to help. Then the water reached his own family. This is Imran Lodhi’s story
Location: Dera Ghazi Khan, Pakistan
Disaster: Pakistan intense monsoon rainfall
Imran Lodhi is a university lecturer with a doctorate in climate change and sustainable development. The 41-year-old was living in Dera Ghazi Khan, a city in south-western Punjab, when floods devastated provinces across Pakistan. Climate change made the monsoon rainfall that caused the floods more intense.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I saw a picture of a two-year-old girl buried in mud. I knew we had to do something’ – This is climate breakdown

articles.author: Raphael Rashid
articles.description:
Broadcaster TV3 appears to cut footage of Thai drag performers and gay Philippine jury spokesperson
Eurovision’s organisers have said they are “surprised and disappointed” that the first Eurovision Asia was altered when it was broadcast in Malaysia, apparently removing LGBTQ+ imagery and people from the show.
The European Broadcasting Union (EBU), the alliance of public broadcasters that owns Eurovision, said it would write to Voxovation, the company producing the Asian contest under licence, and ask it to establish with the Malaysian broadcaster TV3 why it happened.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Eurovision organisers criticise Malaysian removal of LGBT+ footage in first Asian contest

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
Experts say US president may lean toward global affairs after domestic influence curtailed in midterm elections
Donald Trump is embarking on his first overseas trip since his Republican party’s thumping midterm repudiation by US voters, in what may herald a renewed focus on foreign policy for the remainder of his presidency.
The US president will meet his Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, for their first trilateral summit, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) forum in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. Before that, he will land in Manila in the Philippines on Tuesday for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump to embark on Asia trip in apparent foreign policy push before end of term

articles.author: Harry Davies and Yuval Abraham
articles.description:
Upload came as the Israeli military was increasing its reliance on Amazon’s cloud platform to meet the technological demands of its bombardment of Gaza
The Israeli military uploaded 3.5m photos to Amazon’s cloud platform in order to use the US company’s facial recognition technology to analyse images of Palestinians, the Guardian can reveal.
Leaked documents show the expansive catalogue of images was moved into Amazon’s cloud in the early months of Israel’s devastating aerial bombardment and ground offensive in Gaza.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Revealed: Israel uploaded millions of photos to Amazon’s facial recognition platform to track Palestinians

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
articles.description:
Demonstrators tried to block vehicle carrying the baboons, whose capture authorities say is needed to protect both primate and human
The relocation of a troop of baboons in Cape Town to a wildlife sanctuary has triggered furious protests by local people opposed to their capture, which officials argue is necessary to stop human-wildlife conflict in the city.
The 44-member Waterfall troop (named after the area they mainly inhabit) was captured in the southern seaside suburb of Simon’s Town on Friday and Saturday. A second, smaller Seaforth troop is also due to be moved.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Relocation of Cape Town baboons to sanctuary ignites heated protests

articles.author: Megan Davies for MetDesk
articles.description:
Meanwhile, severe thunderstorms bring hailstones the size of baseballs in Argentina
The National Weather Service in the US has confirmed that an EF1 tornado touched down south-east of Newark in the Salem Woods neighbourhood, Delaware, on Thursday. The tornado reached 160 metres wide, had a path length of 4.4 miles (7.1km) and reached estimated peak winds of up to 100mph (161km/h). There were no injuries or fatalities but windows and roofs were damaged on several homes, a large hotel sign fell on to a number of cars, and a semi truck overturned on I95. Although Delaware often experiences a few tornadoes every year, this is only the second time the state has had tornado activity in November since 1950, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The only other November tornado recorded was in 1989.
Severe storms have also resulted in tornadoes in Argentina as well as large hailstones. A round of severe thunderstorms moved through the central Córdoba province on Friday, bringing hailstones up to the size of a baseball (about 7.5cm in diameter). Parts of the province recorded up to 73mm of rainfall in just six hours early on Saturday. Such storms are common at this time of year. Water vapour from the Amazon meeting the Andes quickly condenses, resulting in massive cloud formations often associated with heavy downpours, lightning, tornadoes and large hailstones.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Delaware hit by rare November tornado

articles.author: Donna Ferguson
articles.description:
Exclusive: Public institutions get first chance to bid for rare ‘wonderbook’ of apocalyptic visions and extreme weather
In one illustration, five suns blaze down on Leipzig in 1551. In another, blood rain falls on Rome in 1456. In a third scene, dated 1552, monstrous hailstones batter the Dutch city of Dordrecht during a storm so fierce people feared Judgment Day had come.
Created during the mid-16th century, when earthquakes, storms, floods and other extreme weather events were often interpreted as ominous warnings from God, the Book of Miracles contains 167 paintings of apocalyptic visions, celestial wonders and meteorological phenomena.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It’s like the 16th-century version of doomscrolling’: the Book of Miracles may fetch £1m at auction

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Ahead of Apec summit, PM says ‘Canada is going to move forward either way’ when asked if Chinese investment was leverage in US negotiations
The prime minister of Canada, Mark Carney, said the country could turn to Chinese automakers if trade negotiations with the US president, Donald Trump, failed to preserve an integrated North American auto industry.
Carney’s comments in Cambodia on Monday came ahead of a planned meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping this week in Shenzhen, China, where auto manufacturing is expected to be discussed. The two leaders reached an agreement in January allowing tens of thousands of Chinese electric vehicles into Canada at reduced tariffs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canada could work with Chinese automakers if US trade talks fail, says Carney

articles.author: Dan Collyns and Associated Press
articles.description:
Pontiff delivers forceful speech in Peru as he travels from high in the Andes into the Amazon
Pope Leo XIV has demanded justice for environmental defenders killed for protecting the Amazon and backed efforts by Indigenous peoples to stop their lands from being ravaged by logging and illegal mining.
On the penultimate day of his South American tour, Leo on Sunday travelled into the Peruvian Amazon and channelled one of Pope Francis’s core teachings that links care for the most vulnerable with care for God’s creation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘The blood of these brothers cries out’: Pope Leo demands justice for people killed protecting the Amazon

articles.author: Rory Carroll and agencies
articles.description:
Strikes cast further doubt on peace talks between Tehran and Washington with increasing risk of escalation 
Iran has launched drone attacks against a US military base in Bahrain, casting further doubt on peace talks between Tehran and Washington and raising the spectre of escalation.
Blasts sounded over the Gulf nation on Sunday in the second Iranian drone attack in three days in retaliation for US strikes in Iran.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Iran launches drone attacks against US military base in Bahrain

articles.author: Frances Mao
articles.description:
Iran has targeted airbase in Bahrain in latest resumption of strikes since september
The state-run Bahrain news agency is also carrying the statements of each country in the region responding to Iran’s actions targeting their Gulf neighbour this morning.
Jordan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar have all strongly condemned the attack and expressed solidarity with Bahrain.
The Kingdom affirms that the Iranian attacks constitute a violation of international law and the principles of good neighborliness. The Kingdom stresses the importance of an immediate halt to the blatant Iranian attacks on the countries of the region, and of taking serious steps towards achieving security and stability for the countries of the region and their peoples.
The continuation of these attacks represents a dangerous escalation that will complicate efforts to contain the tension and undermine political and diplomatic endeavors aimed at achieving security and stability in the region.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed the Kingdom of Bahrain’s strongest condemnation of the continued Iranian aggression against its territory, including the attack launched today, Sunday, November 15, 2026, by drones that were intercepted and destroyed by air defense systems in the Kingdom’s airspace.
This comes two days after a similar attack at dawn on Friday, November 13, 2026, by two drones that were also intercepted. The Iranian Revolutionary Guard explicitly claimed responsibility for these attacks. The Ministry praised the efficiency, vigilance, and capability of the Bahrain Defense Force in confronting today’s attack and its complete readiness to deter any aggression.
 

 The Ministry considered these attacks a resumption of Iran’s heinous aggression against the Kingdom and countries in the region, disregarding the provisions of international law and the principles of the UN Charter.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan, Egypt condemn Iranian attack on Bahrain - as it happened

articles.author: Oliver Holmes and Kaamil Ahmed
articles.description:
International court of justice has never before found a state guilty of genocide, and ruling will have implications for case against Israel
The world’s top court will deliver a judgment this week on whether Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, in a landmark case that will set a critical 21st-century benchmark for the gravest of all international crimes.
The closely watched judgment could become one of the most significant moments in international law since the end of the second world war.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: World’s top court to rule if Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya

articles.author: Jonathan Watts; graphics by Sara Fiorillo
articles.description:
People around the world have contended with unprecedented weather events and their fatal effects caused by the climate catastrophe
After the world’s hottest summer since records began in 1850, the death toll from extreme weather in 2026 is already in the high tens of thousands. That is a conservative estimate and is certain to rise much higher.
As Cop31 continues and scientists warn that climate breakdown may be accelerating, the Guardian looks back at a year of droughts, fires and floods as a reminder that, unless the world takes urgent action to cut emissions, this disastrous year will be one of the best of the rest of our lives.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Choking fires, deadly heat and devastating floods: 2026 in extreme weather

articles.author: Ed Walton and Alice Nightingale-Smith for MetDesk
articles.description:
Heavy rain and strong winds have also caused disruption across British Columbia, Canada, over the last week 
Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain. Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November. A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours. In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations.
After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy. This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera. The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia. Further heavy rain is expected to fall in Italy and the Balkans over the next few days, with the latest forecast models indicating an additional 100mm could accumulate widely, while totals close to 200mm are likely in more mountainous areas.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Storm Charles causes floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg and agencies
articles.description:
After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’
The Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded that his entry was “human-written” after a month-long investigation.
Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza cleared of using AI to write prize-winning story

articles.author: Associated Press at the Rafah crossing
articles.description:
Seven-time F1 world champion tours border area and logistics warehouses operated by Egyptian Red Crescent
Lewis Hamilton has visited Egypt’s Rafah border crossing with the Gaza Strip to meet organisations sending humanitarian aid to the territory.
The seven-time Formula One world champion has spoken out about conflict and humanitarian crises in the region, and has called for peace. He has frequently posted on social media about children killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza and called for a ceasefire.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lewis Hamilton visits Egypt’s Rafah crossing and Gaza aid facilities

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Aakash Hassan in Delhi
articles.description:
Former prime minister faces death penalty upon return after being sentenced in absentia over deaths in 2024 uprising
Sheikh Hasina is “confident” she will return to Bangladesh in December, according to exiled members of her party, after the disgraced former prime minister applied for a new passport this week.
Hasina has been living in self-imposed exile since August 2024 when she was toppled from power by a mass uprising against her authoritarian rule. She crossed the border to India, where she has since been allowed to live freely in Delhi.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Disgraced former leader Sheikh Hasina plans return to Bangladesh from exile

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
From the assassinations of her husband and mother-in-law to press stonewalling under Modi, Belonging offers an insider’s account of India’s political evolution
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
Few love stories have been as closely entwined with a nation’s history as that of Sonia and Rajiv Gandhi. The former’s much-awaited political memoir, Belonging, offers a strikingly candid account of her journey from a small town in Italy to the highest echelons of power in India – all for love, she says.
The veteran Congress party leader has been fiercely protective of her personal world. In Belonging, she opens up for the first time about the extraordinary twists and turns of a life that has largely unfolded in full public view. (The Guardian’s Hannah Ellis-Petersen has a rare in-person interview with Gandhi, and you can read an excerpt from the book here.)
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Grenades, grief and a deepening political divide: five takeaways from Sonia Gandhi’s new memoir

articles.author: Cecilia Nowell, Maanvi Singh, Shrai Popat, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Sign up for the Breaking News US email

Lauren Almeida and Dan Milmo
Elon Musk and a host of other tech bosses have called for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement at Nvidia, amid reports the former chief executive is already plotting a return to the chip company just four days after his resignation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump defends commerce secretary Lutnick for allegedly slow-walking Nvidia chip export restrictions – as it happened

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
The US president oscillates between strike threats on Iran and insisting the war ‘militarily is effectively over’
A third US aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East, US Central Command said in a social media post on Monday, making a dramatic show of military might as Donald Trump keeps his options open for next steps in the Iran war.
The USS Theodore Roosevelt brings thousands of additional troops to the Middle East as Trump has oscillated between threatening additional large-scale strikes on Iran and insisting that the more than eight-month-old war “militarily is effectively over”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Third US aircraft carrier brings thousands more troops to Middle East

articles.author: Guthrie Scrimgeour
articles.description:
During the midterm elections, Ni‘ihau backed Democrats for their governors, casting 14 of their 21 votes for Josh Green and Derek Kawakami
The secluded island of Ni‘ihau has long been a Republican stronghold in deep blue Hawai‘i. Ni‘ihauans have an unusual tendency to unanimously support conservative candidates, like in 2020, when all 43 Ni‘ihauan voters cast their ballots for Donald Trump.
This has been the case since as far back as the early 1900s, when Ni‘ihau’s ballots were sometimes relayed to the neighboring island of Kaua‘i via carrier pigeon. The headline of one characteristic 1939 Honolulu Star Bulletin article reads – “Ni‘ihau Casts 59 Votes All For GOP as Usual.” Bush beat Kerry 39-0, Reagan beat Carter 56-1, and Nixon beat Kennedy 99-0.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Even Hawaiʻi’s most Republican island can’t escape the blue wave

articles.author: Ariana Baio
articles.description:
Letter to Warren, likely to chair Senate banking committee, echoes warnings to Democrats moving to investigate Trump
The Trump administration has warned Elizabeth Warren, the senior Democratic senator expected to chair the powerful Senate banking committee, she could face “significant legal consequences” if she fails to preserve records related to investigations into Donald Trump.
US attorney Aaron Reitz of the southern district of Texas sent Warren a warning letter, stating that she appears “eager to wield your future gavel like a tomahawk, hunting for the scalps of President Trump’s private associates”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: DoJ warns Elizabeth Warren of ‘consequences’ unless she preserves Trump records

articles.author: Anna Betts in New York
articles.description:
Mayor axes strategic response group that cracked down on protesters and announces new community safety division
Zohran Mamdani, New York City’s mayor, announced Monday that he was disbanding a city police unit that has faced criticism over the years from civil rights groups who have accused it of using excessive force and unduly aggressive tactics against protesters.
In a video released Monday morning, Mamdani said the move stemmed from a campaign pledge he made to disband the New York City police department’s strategic response group (SRG). “Today, we are keeping that promise,” Mamdani said in the video.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mamdani disbands NYPD unit accused of using excessive force

articles.author: Robert Reich
articles.description:
The party’s big-tent approach has caused post-election feuding in the past. But a pair of singular goals can prevent it
Democrats usually suffer big tent disease. To win, they put together such large coalitions of voters – working class, middle class, Black people, Latinos, women, young people, moderates, liberals – that once they’re in office, intraparty feuds often threaten their agenda.
Will it happen again when they take power in January? I don’t think so. Two outside forces will keep Democrats glued together.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two reasons Democrats can overcome infighting next year | Robert Reich

articles.author: Osita Nwanevu
articles.description:
Americans are at a real point of decision – not election day, but this heady, uncertain moment after
Until 2026, the most important midterm year of the last quarter-century was very probably 2010. Barack Obama famously called the elections a “shellacking” for the Democratic party and he was right. Thanks to a sluggish economic recovery from the Great Recession and backlash against the passage of the Affordable Care Act, Republicans took control of the House with a 63-seat gain – the largest House sweep since the 1940s – and won six seats in the Senate.
But the 2010 midterms were significant well beyond those numbers. It was the first election shaped by the rise of the Tea Party and its blend of rightwing economic populism and xenophobia. Those aligned with the movement lost nearly twice the number of races they won, but the presence of an energized hard-right contingent among Republicans in Congress shaped legislative outcomes for the remainder of Obama’s term and beyond.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Democratic party is at a critical crossroad. Can it do the right thing? | Osita Nwanevu

articles.author: Adria R Walker
articles.description:
Behind the Mississippi senator-elect’s victory is a coalition of groups that didn’t have a lot of money, but had collective power and post-Callais anger
Long before national political leaders and media were paying any attention, long before the Louisiana v Callais supreme court decision gutted the Voting Rights Act, Mississippi organizers were working to grow political participation and improve quality of life in a state that often ranks low on its residents’ health and wellbeing.
Activists’ momentum contributed to Democrat Scott Colom’s historic upset in the midterm elections. A loose coalition of about a dozen, mostly Black-led nonprofits or initiatives rallied residents after Callais, the April decision that set off a flurry of redistricting efforts across southern states. That case was not the sole impetus for organizing efforts across Mississippi, but it turned out thousands in the 20 May “Mississippi Fights Back” rally. Callais became the most recent opportunity to channel people’s frustrations and hopes into action – and to harness previous campaigns that go back years and even decades.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We gotta do something’: the coalition that helped elect Scott Colom to Senate

articles.author: George Chidi in Atlanta
articles.description:
Activists have been shouting about economic issues for years – in January they will expect lawmakers to respond
Stonecrest is resolutely middle class. About six out of 10 of its voters cast ballots in the 2026 election and about 90% of them voted for Democrats, according to election figures. And they have often been overlooked by Georgia’s Republican establishment.
The fundraiser Keisha Lance Bottoms held at the Privi event center and retreat in suburban Atlanta in September didn’t draw a lot of attention. But Stonecrest, by one measure the largest city in the United States with a non-Hispanic Black population above 90%, tends to roll under the radar.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Black voters helped Democrats win in Georgia. Now they expect to be heard

articles.author: Rachel Leingang
articles.description:
Incoming lawmakers have more in common with each other than they have divisions, even across ideological factions
Democrats who won in the midterms, including those in places previously considered off the blue map and those in Democratic strongholds, crafted their campaigns around economic populism and accountability.
Lawmakers in the anti-establishment incoming congressional class have more in common with each other than divisions, even across ideological factions. Voters sent a resounding message to work on affordability and rein in the Trump administration, and Democrats across the party have many more shared goals than Republicans, who face a more existential level of discord.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Progressive versus moderate? Democrats deny party rift as they head into new Congress

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
House members have responded to legitimate criticism with cynicism. Let’s not have another ‘Bernie bros’ moment
Before we get started, some ground rules. You are, of course, completely free to disagree with everything I have to say here. However, doing so might mean that you’re racist, homophobic and/or sexist. (Not to boast, but I have a lot of oppression cards to play.) So, you might want to tread carefully, OK?
That might sound ridiculous, but I don’t make the rules: I’m just taking a page from the corporate Democrat playbook. From Haley Stevens to Hakeem Jeffries, cynically weaponizing identity politics to ward off reasonable criticism seems to be all the rage.
Arwa Mahdawi is a Guardian columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Corporate Democrats are weaponizing identity politics to smear progressives | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: Eric Berger
articles.description:
City has failed to build infrastructure that could reduce threat, and saw 400 fires, 83 injuries and 12 deaths this year
Fires from lithium-ion batteries, which power ebikes and scooters, have become regular occurrences in New York, causing deaths and fear among residents, but the city has failed to build infrastructure that could reduce the threat.
New York has seen a dramatic uptick this year in fires from the batteries. In 2025, there were 292 fires, 51 injuries and one death, according to the New York fire department (FDNY). This year, there have already been more than 400 fires, 83 injuries and 12 deaths.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Enough is enough’: rising number of deadly ebike battery fires spark fear in New York City

articles.author: Bernie Sanders
articles.description:
This is not a personality contest. This is a debate about the future of the Democratic party
The election for Democratic Senate leader between Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen must be understood for what it is.
This is not a personality contest. This is a debate about the future of the Democratic party. It is a debate about whether the Democratic party remains a top-down party dominated by billionaire campaign contributors, inside-the-beltway consultants and 30-second TV ads, or whether we can transform it into a grassroots party of, by and for the working families of our country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What the choice between Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen for Senate leader is all about | Bernie Sanders

articles.author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Aisha Down ; produced by Hana Williams ; senior producer Angus Neale ; executive producer Zoe Hitch

Jensen Huang’s resignation from the AI chipmaker Nvidia has sent shockwaves through the global economy. Huang resigned after reported affairs with an Nvidia executive and a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. The fallout is not over yet, with criticism mounting over the apparent lack of action from the US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick. Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian’s global technology reporter, Aisha Down
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why the Nvidia scandal is far from over - The Latest

Jonathan Freedland speaks to Susan Glasser of the New Yorker about why Trump’s judgment of high-profile men is questionable
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why the Nvidia cheating scandal is bad for Trump | Politics Weekly America
